name: Frederikshavn
title: Ship Thickness Gauging Frederikshavn | Ferries & Repair Yard
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Frederikshavn for ferries, short-sea cargo ships and fishing vessels: docking gauging, ballast tanks, car decks and shell.
h1: Thickness Measurement at Frederikshavn's Repair Yard, Ferry Berths and Quays
intro: Frederikshavn, on the Kattegat coast of northern Jutland, combines a busy ferry harbour with an established ship-repair yard and a fishing and industrial port that has been enlarged in recent years. Ferries to Sweden, Norway and the island of Læsø run from its berths, while short-sea cargo ships, offshore craft and fishing vessels come in for docking and repair. Atlantis brings its technicians from India to the vessel, whether she is sitting in a floating dock at the yard or lying alongside between sailings.

highlights.h: Docking periods at the repair yard
highlights.p: Ørskov Yard's floating docks take ferries, short-sea cargo ships and offshore craft for docking surveys, repairs and conversions. With the hull dry, bottom and side shell, sea chests and the stern area can be gauged before the yard's steel list is settled.

Ro-pax ships on the Gothenburg, Norway and Læsø routes keep tight daily schedules, so gauging is planned for a refit, a seasonal lay-up or the hours between the last arrival and the first departure. Car decks, ramps and machinery-space piping are typical targets.

Trawlers, workboats and small cargo ships lie alongside Frederikshavn's fishing and industrial quays for longer stays. Fishing vessels idle between seasons are a practical time to measure hull plating, fish-hold structure and refrigerated sea-water tanks and piping.

port.h: Frederikshavn: ferries, ship repair and an enlarged harbour
p: Frederikshavn sits on the eastern side of Vendsyssel, the northernmost part of Jutland, facing the Kattegat a short distance south of Skagen. Its harbour is open-coast rather than a fjord or river port, approached directly from the Kattegat and protected by breakwaters, and the small tidal range of these waters means berthing depends on wind and pilotage rather than the state of the tide. The town has always lived from the sea: ferries to Sweden and Norway, a naval station, a fishing fleet and shipbuilding and repair have all shaped the waterfront. The harbour has been extended with new quays, basins and reclaimed land, intended to attract larger ships, heavy industry and recycling work, and the deeper water has widened the range of vessels that can come alongside.

Ferry traffic is the most visible part of the port. Stena Line's crossing to Gothenburg has run for decades, ro-pax services connect the town with Norway, and smaller ferries cross to Læsø out in the Kattegat. Beyond the ferries, the harbour handles short-sea general cargo and bulk, project cargo for industry in northern Jutland, offshore and service vessels, and the trawlers and seiners of the fishing harbour. Many ships come specifically for the repair yard: short-sea tankers, ro-ro ships, offshore vessels and ferries from Danish, Norwegian and Swedish operators book docking slots here, and some arrive for conversion or life-extension work rather than routine maintenance. Ship recycling has also been carried out in the enlarged harbour, adding a further reason for older tonnage to call.

Timing in Frederikshavn follows two calendars. Ferry operators schedule dockings and refits in the quieter months outside the summer peak, so inspection work at the yard and on the ferry berths tends to cluster from autumn to spring. Fishing vessels follow their own seasons and quotas, coming in for maintenance when the fishery they work is closed. The Kattegat can be rough in winter, with strong westerly and northerly winds, but the harbour itself is sheltered and does not normally see ice, so work alongside and in dock carries on through the year. For a team travelling from India the practical constraint is notice: a docking slot is fixed weeks ahead, which leaves time for visas, while a ferry's overnight window is predictable but short.

facilities.h: Docks, quays and lay-by berths for gauging in Frederikshavn
p: The repair yard is the centre of gauging work here. Ørskov Yard operates floating docks and repair quays in the harbour, has handled dockings, repairs and conversions for many years, and has invested in a further floating dock. A ship in dock gets staging, lighting and ventilation through the yard, and the team works to the TM plan beside the attending surveyor, marking substantial corrosion and suspect welds on the steel so that the yard's planners can schedule renewal while the ship is still dry. Readings from the tanks most likely to need steel are passed over first, so cutting and fabrication can start early in the stay.

Outside the yard, gauging is done afloat. Ferries lie at their linkspans overnight and can be measured on car decks and in machinery spaces between the last arrival and the first departure, or more fully during a planned lay-up. The industrial and bulk quays suit cargo ships discharging or waiting for repairs to begin, and fishing vessels can be measured at their usual berths between trips. Ships waiting for a docking slot sometimes lie at a lay-by berth for several days, and that wait is a useful time to gauge ballast tanks and decks so the docking starts with the steel list already drafted.
list: Ørskov Yard floating docks — bottom and side shell, sea chests, rudder and stern-frame gauging on ships in for docking surveys.
Ørskov Yard repair quays — tank, deck and piping measurement during afloat repairs, conversions and life-extension work.
Ferry linkspans — car-deck plating, ramp structure and machinery-space piping on ro-pax ships in overnight windows or lay-up.
Industrial and bulk quays — holds, ballast tanks and deck on short-sea cargo ships alongside for cargo or waiting for the yard.
Fishing harbour — hull plating, fish-hold structure and sea-water piping on trawlers and seiners between trips or seasons.
Lay-by berths in the enlarged harbour — pre-docking or pre-purchase gauging on ships idle before a yard slot or sale.

context.h: Ferry inspections, recycling rules and port state control at Frederikshavn
p: Port state control in Frederikshavn is the responsibility of the Danish Maritime Authority under the Paris MoU. Ro-pax ferries on regular international routes also fall under the EU's directive on inspections of ro-ro passenger ships and high-speed passenger craft in regular service, which brings inspections at set intervals, so the condition of car decks, bow and stern doors, ramps and the steel around them is looked at often. Thickness data from a docking or refit, set out on the class formats, gives the operator a record showing that wastage is being tracked from one period to the next rather than discovered at an inspection.

The harbour's interest in recycling makes the EU Ship Recycling Regulation more than background here. Ships flying the flag of an EU member state may only be recycled at facilities on the European List, and non-EU ships of 500 GT and above calling at an EU port must hold an Inventory of Hazardous Materials, which port state control officers check. Owners weighing whether an older ship is worth another renewal survey start from the same evidence: how much steel the next survey will demand. Gauging at a Frederikshavn docking answers that question, and the EU ETS from 2024 and FuelEU Maritime from 2025 give a further reason to review older tonnage.

jobs.p: Work in Frederikshavn falls into docking jobs and alongside jobs. Docking jobs are planned with the yard: the superintendent sends the TM plan and previous reports, the team arrives as the ship goes into dock, and readings follow the yard's sequence so that blasting, staging and steel renewal are not held up. Alongside jobs are shorter and depend on the ship's timetable, whether that is a ferry's overnight lay-over, a cargo ship's discharge or a trawler's days between trips. Either way, readings are released as each area is finished, so decisions on repairs are made while the yard and the ship are still within reach. Typical requests include:
list: Docking-survey gauging of bottom and side shell and sea chests on a ro-pax ferry in one of the yard's floating docks.
Car-deck and stern-ramp measurement with magnetic particle testing at the hinge lugs on a ferry during her winter refit.
Pre-docking gauging of ballast tanks on a short-sea tanker lying at a lay-by berth while she waits for her yard slot.
Hull plating and fish-hold gauging on a pelagic trawler between seasons, ahead of an intermediate survey.
Condition gauging on an offshore vessel arriving for conversion, to show the owner how much original steel can stay.

logistics: Aalborg Airport is the closest airport with international connections, and a regional train runs from Aalborg to Frederikshavn; Copenhagen and Billund are the main long-haul gateways, with onward rail or a domestic flight to Aalborg. Entry to the yard is through its own gate and safety induction, arranged with the yard by the superintendent, while the ferry and cargo quays fall under ISPS controls handled by the ship's agent. The team travels from India on Schengen visas, so docking dates should reach us as soon as the yard slot is confirmed.

faqs.q: Can you work in a floating dock at Ørskov Yard on behalf of the owner?
faqs.a: Yes. We are engaged by the owner or ship manager and work alongside the yard rather than for it. The superintendent arranges staging, lighting, ventilation and gas-free certificates with the yard, and we follow the TM plan agreed with the attending surveyor. Areas of substantial or excessive corrosion are marked on the plating so the yard can start planning renewal before the ship leaves the dock.

faqs.q: How much can be measured on a ferry overnight in Frederikshavn?
faqs.a: A focused scope: a section of car deck, the stern ramp and its hinges, or a run of machinery-space piping. The hours between the last arrival and the first sailing are predictable, but cleaning and preparing reading points takes time, so we agree a priority list with the chief engineer in advance. Wider scopes covering tanks and shell plating are better planned for the refit or the docking.

faqs.q: Do you gauge fishing vessels as well as merchant ships?
faqs.a: We do. Steel trawlers and seiners need hull, deck and fish-hold plating measured for their own surveys and for owners planning a refit or a sale. Fishing vessels have their own corrosion patterns, with refrigerated sea-water tanks and constantly wet fish holds driving corrosion behind insulation and coatings. The best time is when the vessel is laid up between fisheries and the holds and tanks can be emptied and dried.

faqs.q: Is thickness gauging useful before deciding to recycle an older ship?
faqs.a: It is often the deciding evidence. If the next renewal survey looks likely to call for heavy steel renewal, the owner may choose to sell or recycle instead, and gauging the main structural members ahead of that survey gives a realistic steel estimate. Recycling itself also needs an Inventory of Hazardous Materials, which is a separate survey from thickness measurement and not one that we carry out.
